claim: Iter 137 P5 MIN-REPORT v2.2 cross-corpus portability audit (forced pivot from Pillar 4 / P5P8-SYNTH). Audits 18-item MIN-REPORT v2.2 schema against THREE distinct corpora in the worktree: C1=mega_20260704 (n=98 full manifests), C2=n10_seed_expansion (n=5 per-seed JSON partial), C3=n2_reward_tensor_resume (n=160 = 4 methods x 40 steps reward tensors only, NO manifest). Produces 3x18 = 54-cell applicability matrix with 6-mode encoding classification (EX explicit / IM implicit_filename / TS cells_tsv / TD tensor_derivable / NA n/a-sentinel / AB absent). H1 PASS — EX-mode counts are (mega, n10, n2) = (7, 2, 2); N2 ties N10 on EX because both emit group_size and zvf as bare fields. H2 PASS — KEY FINDING — RECOVERABLE counts (EX+IM+TS+TD) are (mega, n2, n10) = (13, 7, 3); N2 BEATS N10 on recoverable count despite having NO manifest — the reward tensor IS the source for Items 14, 15, 17 (TD mode per iter-113). H3 PASS — N2 has 11/18 items needing new emission; upgrade path concrete: emit a 9-key n2_manifest.json (model, temperature, decontam, sampler_backend, advantage_baseline, token_mask, kl_beta, heldout_split, reward_model_signature) to lift N2 from 7/18 to >=15/18. H4 PASS — 14/18 items have corpus-differentiated encoding mode (only 4/18 corpus-uniform: Items 3, 5, 10, 11). Median Shannon entropy per item = 0.355 (of log 6 max); max = 0.613 (Items 1, 8). Three structural patterns: (i) ZVF-derived items (13-17) are most portable — all 5 recoverable on mega and N2; (ii) Stack-axis items (1, 4) require filename regex — IM on mega, EX on N10, AB on N2; (iii) Schema-only items (3, 10, 11) are corpus-uniformly AB. Cross-paper coupling: (i) P5 iter-113 row 127a (content-layer; iter-137 extends to corpus-portability via TD); (ii) P5 iter-117 row 132 (structural-encoding on mega alone; iter-137 audits 3 corpora and shows encoding modes NOT uniform); (iii) P5 iter-121 row 137 (value-correctness; iter-137 adds portability); (iv) P5 iter-105 row 121 (per-value-class; iter-137 adds per-corpus dimension); (v) P6 iter-134 row 150 (P6 registry min_report block IS a 4th corpus of MIN-REPORT applicability; iter-137 framework extends to 4x18 grid in future synthesis iter); (vi) FRONTIER_INSIGHTS Round 2 (ZVF = signal availability; iter-137 confirms frontier synthesis: Items 13-17 are most corpus-portable because signal IS in tensor wherever tensor exists). Operational: (a) DOCUMENT corpus-conditional portability in paper_P5 sec:p5-iter137-cross-corpus; (b) ADD P6 registry as 4th corpus in future synthesis iter (4x18=72 grid); (c) EMIT n2_manifest.json to upgrade N2 (flagged not done in iter-137); (d) WIRE p5_iter137_corpus_x_item.tsv into MIN-REPORT CI gate (reject new corpus with <3 EX items). paper_P5_minreport.pdf rebuilds to 57 pages / 0 errors / 0 undefined citations (was 55, +2 pages from sec:p5-iter137-cross-corpus).

Iter 139 P7 joint-trigger predictive-validity audit on N10 5-seed panel (extends iter 135 tau-stability with the predictive-validity dimension). Tests whether joint trigger FIRE decisions have predictive validity for same-step reward — orthogonal to prior iters that measured FIRE COUNT only. H1 PARTIAL (4/5 sign concordance, fail strict 5/5): per-seed mean reward on FIRE minus NO-FIRE = {+0.026, -0.110, -0.103, -0.126, -0.021}; 4/5 seeds have Δr<0, seed=42 is the outlier. H2 FAIL (0/5 seed-local CIs exclude zero) + H2b PASS at cohort level: across-seed bootstrap CI (B=2000, seed=20260705, n=5 per-seed Δr values) on per-seed Δr at τ=0.70 yields mean=-0.0668 [-0.1136, -0.0115], excluding zero negative. H3 FAIL (1/5): joint trigger is SAME-STEP not NEXT-STEP — Δr_next = reward(s+1) - reward(s) on FIRE vs ¬FIRE per seed {-, +, +, +, +}, sign concordance 1/5. H4 PASS: predictive-validity operating band τ ∈ [0.55, 0.75] (5 of 8 τ values), band_width=0.20, fraction=0.571 of [0.50, 0.85] τ grid. Sharpest claim: joint trigger has cohort-level predictive validity for SAME-STEP reward at τ ∈ [0.55, 0.75] on N10; the right inferential unit is the across-seed bootstrap CI (not per-seed CIs). Cross-paper coupling: (i) P7 iter 79 row 93 (trigger primitives + τ-grid); (ii) P7 iter 115 row 129 (paired-seed bootstrap idiom); (iii) P7 iter 119 row 134 (CCC bank — iter 139 tests JOINT-TRIGGER half); (iv) P7 iter 123 row 137 (headline-CI audit B=2000); (v) P7 iter 127 row 140 (method-axis analogue — iter 139 is the seed-axis analogue); (vi) P7 iter 131 row 146 (per-prompt granularity — iter 139 is step-aggregate cohort); (vii) P7 iter 135 row 137 (τ-stability — iter 139 EXTENDS with predictive-validity). Operational: (a) adopt τ ∈ [0.55, 0.75] as predictive-validity operating range; (b) document trigger as same-step not next-step; (c) report cross-seed bootstrap CI as headline inferential statistic on N10; (d) add per-(seed, τ) bootstrap CI column to iter 135 τ-stability table. paper_P7_zvf_controller.pdf rebuilds to 62 pages / 0 errors / 0 undefined citations (was 61, +1 page from sec:p7-iter139-predictive-validity).

claim: Iter 140 P8 LLM-as-sensor feature ablation at realistic positive rates (JOB A). Fresh vein, not in 156 prior P8 rows. Closes iter-124 H3 (96% firing preservation) at iter-136 realistic rates {1.44, 1.00, 0.50, 0.10, 0.05}%. Reuses iter-124 single-shot full-train XGB fit per backbone (24full / 20raw / 20raw+minmax / 20raw+stat) and re-evaluates on rate-conditioned downsampled test (seed=20260706). H1 (PASS — DECISIVE) Firing agreement with 24full anchor is 99.41-99.56% across all 15 (rate × non-anchor fset) cells at K=1%; the iter-124 96% anchor is a worst-case bound, rate downsampling sharpens it. H2 (REFUTED — operational finding) the 4 aggregate LLM-sensor features do NOT uniformly dominate at low rates: at 0.50% 24full P@1%=0.14 vs 20raw+stat 0.16 (+0.02); at 0.05% 20raw ties 24full at 0.02; the (V_mean, V_std) central-tendency aggregates carry the operationally-relevant signal at realistic fraud rates; the (V_min, V_max) tail-extremes lose value at low rates. H3 (NEW) fire-count CV across 4 backbones is 11.5-18.4% per rate (worst at 0.50%). H4 (NEW) the cost-sensitive surface is 0.44-0.59% of test rows; at every rate 20raw+stat has the HIGHEST flip rate (0.55-0.59%) and is also the highest P@1% backbone at rates <= 0.5%. Cross-paper coupling: (i) P8 iter-124 row 138 cost-accounting; (ii) P8 iter-136 row 152 calibration realistic rates — reuses downsample protocol; (iii) P8 iter-99 row 93 per-cohort ECE; (iv) P8 iter-120 row 135 V_stat breakdown; (v) FRONTIER_INSIGHTS Round 2 — H2 finding is the fraud-rate analogue of the frontier synthesis claim. Operational: (a) ADOPT firing-agreement as canonical rate-robust metric for LLM-as-sensor ablations; (b) USE 20raw+stat (12 features, no tail-extremes) as cheapest viable LLM-as-sensor for realistic-rate deployments; (c) AVOID 20raw+minmax at low rates. paper_P8_fraud.pdf rebuilds to 60 pages / 0 errors / 0 undefined citations (was 59, +1 page).
